sections.h2: What does the Burke County Register of Deeds do when a house sells?
sections.html:
The office keeps the permanent public record of who owns land in Burke County, and your deed has to reach it before the buyer's ownership counts against outsiders. The county describes the office as the keeper of a standardized, permanent record of real estate ownership and transfers. It records deeds, deeds of trust, cancellations, plats, powers of attorney and assumed names, and it also issues birth and death certificates, marriage licenses and notary commissions.

Recording order matters. Under G.S. 47-18, a conveyance does not bind lien creditors or later buyers for value until it is registered in the county where the land sits, and priority follows the time of registration. A Burke County deed that sits in a drawer protects nobody.

Wills and estate files are a different matter. The county's FAQ says estate questions and court actions go to the Clerk of Court, not to the register of deeds.

sections.h2: Where is the Burke County Register of Deeds and when is it open?
sections.html:
The office is in Morganton on South Green Street, and it is open Monday through Friday from 8 a.m. to 5 p.m., closed on observed county holidays. The county directory lists the mailing address as P.O. Box 936, Morganton, NC 28680, and the phone as 828-764-9340. Two county pages print slightly different street numbers for the building, so confirm the door before you drive a closing package over.

The Register of Deeds is elected by Burke County voters every two years under G.S. 161-1. Staff cannot give legal advice about what a deed should say, so a closing attorney normally prepares the document and brings it in.

  • Walk-in recording at the Morganton office on weekdays
  • Mail-in recording to the P.O. Box
  • Electronic recording through approved submitters
  • Online search of real estate records from the county site

sections.h2: What does recording a deed cost in Burke County?
sections.html:
A general instrument such as a deed costs $26.00 for the first 15 pages, and a deed of trust costs $64.00 for the first 35 pages, each with $4.00 for every extra page. Those numbers come from the county's published fee schedule for FY 24-25, which cites G.S. 161-10, and they match the uniform statewide schedule.

Selected recording fees on the Burke County fee schedule (FY 24-25)
ItemFee as printed
Instruments in general$26.00 first 15 pages, $4.00 each added page
Deeds of trust or mortgages$64.00 first 35 pages, $4.00 each added page
Satisfaction of a deed of trustNo fee
Plats$21.00 per sheet or page
Additional instruments in one document$10.00 each
Nonstandard document$25.00 on top of recording fees
Certified copy of an instrument$5.00, plus $2.00 per added page
Plain copies$.25 per page

The nonstandard charge applies when a document ignores the state's formatting rules, so have the preparer follow G.S. 161-14 margins and type size. A released mortgage costs nothing to cancel, which helps when a seller is clearing an old loan before closing.

sections.h2: Who pays the excise tax on a Burke County deed?
sections.html:
The seller pays it, and the register collects it at the counter before the deed is recorded. State law sets the rate at one dollar for each $500 of value or fraction of it, and says the transferor pays the register of deeds in the county where the land lies (G.S. 105-228.30). The Burke County fee schedule words the same rate as $2.00 per thousand, with $1.00 charged up to $500.

Half of the money stays with the county general fund, and the other half goes to the state through monthly remittance. Because the stamp tracks the sale price or value in the deed, it is one of the closing line items that rises with the home's price. Ask your closing attorney for the exact stamp amount on your settlement statement rather than estimating it.

sections.h2: Why does the Burke County tax office sign a deed before it is recorded?
sections.html:
Burke County requires a delinquent tax certification before the register will accept a deed that transfers real property. The county's form cites G.S. 161-31, which lets commissioners direct the register not to take a deed unless the tax collector certifies that no delinquent ad valorem taxes are owed. The current version of the form was revised in April 2026.

The form asks for specific facts, so gather them before closing day:

  • GIS PIN or REID number for each parcel being transferred
  • Grantor and grantee names, plus the grantee's mailing address
  • The current owner per tax records and the property's physical address
  • Sale price and acreage being transferred
  • Whether a single-wide or double-wide mobile home is included
  • Whether the land is in the Present Use Value program, and whether the new owner will stay in it
  • Any personal property included, such as vehicles, boats or farm equipment

Tax office staff then fill in a year-by-year grid of taxes due and deferred taxes. Questions go to the Burke County Tax Administrator's office at 828-764-9430, or by email to collections@burkenc.org. The county FAQ adds that fixing an error in a recorded deed means drawing a new deed, sending it through the tax office for certification, and then filing it with the register.

sections.h2: Can a Burke County deed be recorded electronically?
sections.html:
Yes. The register accepts electronic documents through Simplifile and Corporation Service Company (CSC), according to the county's eRecording page and FAQ. A closing attorney or title company sets up an account, submits the package without leaving the office, and receives the recorded document back electronically right after recording.

For a seller who is signing in another state, electronic recording can shorten the wait between signing and the buyer's ownership becoming official. Ask the closing attorney whether the firm submits through one of these platforms, and whether the tax certification has already been cleared.

sections.h2: What should Burke County sellers know about the local market and the 2027 revaluation?
sections.html:
Burke County sits in the western section of the state, in the mountain region, and it is preparing for a 2027 property tax revaluation. The county posted a notice of a public hearing for November 16, 2026, on the proposed schedule of values and present use schedule of values for that project, with both schedules available at the tax office and on the county site.

The county website describes an economy built on industrial products, with technological, furniture, medical, chemical, machine component and textile manufacturers, and it notes that the western campus of the North Carolina School of Science and Mathematics and Western Piedmont Community College are located here.

  • Population estimate for July 1, 2025: 88,655, with 41,669 housing units
  • Owner-occupied housing unit rate for 2020-2024: 74.5%
  • Median value of owner-occupied homes for 2020-2024: $185,400
  • Median gross rent for 2020-2024: $884, and median household income $58,592
  • Land area: 506.24 square miles, per Census Bureau QuickFacts

Close to a quarter of residents are 65 or older (23.2%), which is relevant to the state's elderly and disabled homestead exclusion. For the 2026 tax year the income limit for that program is $38,800, per the Department of Revenue's application form.

faqs.q: How much does it cost to record a deed at the Burke County Register of Deeds?
faqs.a: A standard deed costs $26.00 for up to 15 pages, then $4.00 per extra page, per the county's fee schedule. A deed of trust runs $64.00 for the first 35 pages. The excise tax on the sale is a separate charge paid by the seller.

faqs.q: Can I record a deed in Burke County without going through the tax office?
faqs.a: No for deeds that transfer real property. The county's delinquent tax certification form, based on G.S. 161-31, says the register will not accept the deed until the tax collector certifies no delinquent taxes. Submit the form with the PIN or REID number and sale details.

faqs.q: Does the Burke County Register of Deeds handle probate and wills?
faqs.a: No. The county FAQ points estate and court questions to the Clerk of Court, whose number it lists as 828-433-3200.

faqs.q: Who pays the transfer tax in a Burke County sale?
faqs.a: The seller does. State law has the transferor pay the register of deeds before the deed is recorded, at one dollar for each $500 of value. Your settlement statement will show the stamp amount.

faqs.q: Are Burke County real estate records available online?
faqs.a: Yes. The county FAQ states that real estate records can be viewed online, and the register's office also accepts electronic recording through Simplifile and CSC. For anything the online index does not answer, call 828-764-9340 on weekdays between 8 a.m. and 5 p.m.
